admission.justification: Reporting branch movement when the re-read tip is unchanged would conceal a real Git hook or lock refusal. Re-reading the intended ref distinguishes an actual concurrent tip change from a failed update at the admitted tip and preserves Git's diagnostic in the latter case.

rows.statement: A failed ref update reports a moved branch only if its tip moved and otherwise preserves Git refusal text.
rows.applicability: A failed ref update during publication or take-back.
conditions: The intended ref was re-read after the failure.
exclusions: A rejection with no moved tip; Git's own text is kept.

rows.facet: A refused ref transaction is reported with Git's own text.

admission.justification: Waiting on a lock error that can never clear would stall publication indefinitely.

rows.statement: Only a lock error that would block is waited for and every other lock error is refused immediately.
conditions: The lock error says another holder would block the attempt.
exclusions: Every other lock error, which waiting cannot cure.

rows.facet: Only a lock error that would block is waited for.

admission.justification: At least one proof names this invariant's exact behavior at the candidate.

rows.statement: Lifecycle commit publication runs no commit hooks, including the direct-landing memory commit.
rows.applicability: Commit-object publication for ordinary, direct and prepared routes.
conditions: The route is the shared commit-tree primitive.
exclusions: Prepared memory publication, which keeps ordinary Git hooks.

rows.facet: Direct landing commits the judged tree with no commit hooks.

admission.justification: The gate's evaluation can take a minute; without this binding a file written meanwhile, or content staged only in the repository's index, would be committed to a leaf's memory without the validator or the worklist having judged it.

rows.statement: The tree a converted leaf's closeout commits to memory is the tree its gate judged: every write the closeout itself makes to memory content -- the metadata refresh, the history closing and the ledger cache's ignore rule -- is on disk before the tree is read; a working tree or index that changed while the gate ran is refused before the memory commit's Git mutation; and the commit is staged from the judged tree object and proved against it, so a file written after that check stays an uncommitted change and is never committed unjudged.
rows.applicability: The memory commit of a converted leaf's worktree closeout.
conditions: The memory tree is converted, so the closeout holds a judged tree.
exclusions: Unconverted memory, which has no judged tree and is staged from the working tree as before.
Direct landing is outside this invariant: its commit is bound to its admission snapshot, not to the tree its gate judged.

The ledger memory.md, which the commit excludes. The cache preparation removes it from the repository's index before the judged-tree check; that is the one index write that precedes the memory commit's mutation.
The retired database-era realization site; the obligation is recorded on converted memory only.

rows.facet: A card rewritten in place while the gate runs is refused before the memory commit's Git mutation, with the closing and .gitignore restored; on the rerun the commit's tree and its proof's expected tree are the judged tree, and files written after the check stay uncommitted.

admission.justification: A plain copy of an index is a new file with a new time, so Git trusts every entry's recorded stat data: a same-size rewrite in that second keeps its old blob in the capture, and a cached knowledge index of the old content is served as current.

rows.statement: A disposable capture taken through a copy of a repository's Git index copies the index together with its file's modification time, bytes and time read from one open file, so Git still compares by content a file that was rewritten in the second the index was written. The knowledge index's directory key and the closeout's staging snapshot therefore never answer such a rewrite from its old blob.
rows.applicability: Every capture of a working tree that starts from a copy of the repository's own Git index.
conditions: The repository has an index file to copy.
exclusions: Staging through the repository's own index, where Git's own check applies.

rows.facet: After a same-size rewrite in the second the index was written the directory key changes, the cache builds a new index that holds the rewritten statement, and an unchanged tree still reuses its index.
The staging snapshot taken through the copied index reads the card as rewritten in that second, and equals the exact tree.
The copy uses the source index modification time and a mutated copy-time implementation fails the intended recheck.
A same-size same-second rewrite changes the shared candidate tree on both code and memory sides.

admission.justification: Dropping index flags, intent-to-add or sparse entries during publication or refusal would lose staged work.

rows.statement: Publication and refusal preserve index flags, intent-to-add entries outside the commit and sparse-checkout entries.
rows.applicability: Index restoration across publication and refusal.
conditions: The index holds flags, intent-to-add entries or sparse-checkout entries a tree cannot record.
exclusions: Entries the caller staged for the commit itself; those follow the judged tree.

rows.facet: Index flags, intent-to-add and sparse entries survive publication and refusal.

admission.justification: Publishing over an unresolved merge would write a partial tree as if it were judged.

rows.statement: An unfinished native action is refused before the index is asked for a tree, including a real unresolved merge.
conditions: The repository index or worktree holds an unfinished action.
exclusions: A clean repository; the check is then a no-op.

rows.facet: An unfinished action or empty message publishes nothing.

admission.justification: Take-back that overwrites a concurrent foreign commit would destroy another writer's commit.

rows.statement: Take-back retains an expected-old compare-and-swap and only unpublished refusal cancellations can replace themselves with the same request.
rows.applicability: Take-back and replacement of publication attempts.
conditions: The expected-old value was captured with the admitted parent.
exclusions: An unpublished refusal, which may replace itself with the same request.

admission.justification: A faster read could otherwise miss flagged changes or mutate the user index that a later commit relies on; the reference-state matrix and explicit original-index assertions pin both hazards.

rows.statement: The worktree's real index, its files and the user's work are never changed.
rows.applicability: Candidate-tree observations through the shared worktree_candidate_tree owner, for code and external memory repositories.
conditions: Git evidence is retained only for entries matching HEAD; staged changed/add/remove entries are restored before working files are added.
Assume-unchanged and skip-worktree flags are cleared only on the copy; objects are written into the addressed repository so candidates can be pinned.
Ignored staged paths absent from HEAD stay absent, and explicit caller-owned derived exclusions are preserved.
exclusions: Ordinary staging or commit operations intentionally using the real index.
An unchanged file is not reconverted merely because attributes, filters or core.autocrlf changed after its recorded stat evidence; the approved capture follows what that real index stages.

rows.facet: An unusable index copy uses the existing full private capture and returns its exact tree rather than guessed state.
Private-index capture matches the previous reference across the listed staged/unstaged/ignored/flagged states and exclusions while preserving real-index state.
Index flags cannot hide working changes, and the original flags/index stay untouched.

admission.justification: Realized across 2 files that together perform the obligation.

rows.statement: A switched HEAD plus failed expected-old take-back may leave the published memory commit reachable while ordinary closeout restores its preparatory files.
conditions: Publication raised after creating a reachable commit, HEAD switched, and expected-old take-back did not remove that commit.
exclusions: Ordinary unpublished refusal and validation after a successful publication return; their restoration boundaries are separate.

admission.justification: A message git would abort on, committed with different content than git commit -m stores, would ship an unintended message.

rows.statement: The publication message matches real git commit -m cleanup behavior and refuses invalid modes and messages made empty by cleanup.
rows.applicability: Publication message cleanup and its refusals.
conditions: The repository's configured cleanup mode and comment character apply.
exclusions: A message file path; the primitive takes one message value.

rows.facet: The stored message equals what git commit -m stores, and an aborted message is refused.

admission.justification: Publication that changes the message, index shape or hook behavior would make the committed object differ from the reviewed one.

rows.statement: Publication preserves the ruled message, index flags and hook behavior and names real ref/lock failures.
rows.applicability: Publication message, index and hook behavior on the shared primitive.
conditions: The repository pins the cleanup mode, comment character and hook policy.
exclusions: Prepared routes, which keep their no-verify or ordinary-hook policy.

admission.justification: Negative controls expose loss of expected-old take-back, replacement narrowing and cleanup protection, which could otherwise overwrite concurrent commits or remove protected content while ordinary successful tests stay green.

rows.statement: Tests catch loss of expected-old take-back, replacement narrowing and cleanup validation.
rows.applicability: Take-back and replacement controls under test.
conditions: The expected-old value is wrong or the selection is terminal.
exclusions: A clean success; no control fires.

admission.justification: Realized across 2 files that together perform the obligation.

rows.statement: The closeout docstring states that a partial publication with failed expected-old takeback may retain a reachable commit while preparations restore, whereas proof failure after successful publication return leaves preparations in place.
rows.applicability: The ordinary closeout's documentation of its publication and preparation-restoration boundary.
conditions: The documentation distinguishes publication raising after partial ref movement from proof validation after a successful publication return.
exclusions: A claim that documentation repairs the retained runtime race or publication policy.

admission.justification: Publishing a commit object against a moved or foreign parent would put an unreviewed tree on the branch.

rows.statement: publish_tree_commit binds the admitted parent and intended ref.
conditions: The admitted parent and intended ref were captured before object creation.
exclusions: A caller-provided ref path outside the admitted contract.

admission.justification: Capture/index isolation, one resolved pair, confirmed conversion reuse, consumed-byte memo admission and literal patch binding each close a different way an optimization could return source/intent under the wrong observed identity; none alone preserves the complete live review operation.

rows.title: Exact live reviewer reuse
rows.guarantee: Live reviewer optimizations share one source resolution and capture owner, reuse only exactly confirmed conversion/view inputs, and bind every addressed patch to its literal path, while preserving real-index isolation, actual consumed task bytes, publication rechecks and failed-read refusals. No faster path supplies a comparison, worklist or patch under inputs it did not observe.

admission.justification: Reusing a conversion without exact inputs could silently compare another code/memory baseline; the mismatch matrix protects reuse while avoiding repeated materialization of an already held tree.

rows.statement: A converted base tree is written only when Git does not hold it.
rows.applicability: Live tree comparisons whose before memory is converted from a legacy base.
conditions: The latest comparison record binds the same memory commit, pinned conversion version and paired code commit.
git cat-file confirms the recorded root object is a tree before reuse.
exclusions: A missing tree or mismatched conversion inputs retains the existing conversion/materialization behavior.
This does not skip capture of either live candidate or replace recorded comparison numbering and pins.

rows.facet: Matching held conversion inputs avoid mktree/hash-object and preserve the full body; each mismatched input and absent tree recomputes.
